fact: Gauteng Department of e-Government reported that 6,461 government employees received digital skills training in its 2025/26 reporting period.

Deputy Minister Nzuza says Home Affairs set aside R4 million for training, with a Digital Literacy Programme for all staff rolling out over 2025 to 2028 covering information literacy, collaboration tools, devices and software, cyber security and content management.

The Minister of Public Service and Administration's written reply says the National School of Government's free online digital courses (AI Fluency, Cyber Security Awareness, Mobile Digital Literacy, Digital Art of Facilitation) had trained 4,725 public servants.

fact: The Department of Public Service and Administration reports that the National School of Government and Microsoft South Africa signed a memorandum of agreement aiming to train 100,000 public servants in digital literacy, AI and cybersecurity on NSG Learner Management Platforms.

President Ramaphosa, quoted in the National School of Government annual report, welcomed the launch of the National AI Skilling Initiative to provide AI skills training for public servants, with a Microsoft, NSG and NEMISA MoU still to be signed.
